description: Minimum evidence authority per claim type. Read by scripts/ledger_core.py. A claim type is satisfied when ANY clause in any_of is satisfied; a clause is satisfied when EVERY requirement in it is met by distinct ACTIVE evidence records (one record never counts twice in the same clause). Extend per investigation with ledger.authority_extensions, never by editing this file during an investigation.

compiler.description: A real compiler or build system was run on the code and its result recorded.

linter.description: A linter was run and its output recorded.

type-checker.description: A type checker was run and its output recorded.

static-analysis.description: Reading or analyzing code or a binary without executing it: source reading, disassembler, decompiler, analyzer, cross-references. Never establishes that code executed.

byte-inspection.description: Direct inspection of bytes: hex dump, hashes, magic numbers, strings, offsets.

version-diff.description: Comparison between two identified versions of an artifact.

unit-test.description: Unit tests executed. Establishes behavior of the unit in the test environment only, not of the packaged artifact.

integration-test.description: Integration tests executed across real component boundaries.

property-test.description: Property-based tests executed with recorded seeds or example counts.

fuzzing.description: Fuzzing campaign executed with recorded corpus, duration and seed.

packaged-artifact-test.description: The built, packaged or shipped artifact itself was exercised in its target form.

benchmark.description: A benchmark executed with recorded environment, repetitions and variance.

runtime-trace.description: Observation of actual execution: trace, log, debugger, profiler, instrumentation.

controlled-mutation.description: One variable was changed on purpose while others were held fixed, and the effect was observed by execution. Includes reproduce -> change -> revert experiments on code.

emulation.description: Execution under an emulator or simulator. Not evidence about real hardware or the real world unless the emulator's fidelity for this behavior is itself established.

round-trip-comparison.description: Parse/serialize (or decode/encode) round trip compared byte for byte or field for field with the original.

schema-validation.description: Data validated against an explicit schema by a tool.

independent-calculation.description: The value was recomputed by a tool or route independent of the one that produced it.

numerical-test.description: Finite numerical cases evaluated. Evidence for or against a general claim; never a proof of one.

counterexample-search.description: A bounded, recorded search for counterexamples. A found counterexample refutes; an empty search only bounds where none exists.

sat-smt.description: SAT or SMT solver result over a stated encoding.

formal-proof.description: Machine-checked proof (Lean, Coq, Isabelle or similar) that the checker accepted.

formalization-review.description: Review confirming that a formal statement matches the original informal claim.

reviewed-proof.description: A written proof reviewed by someone other than its author.

primary-source.description: Original document, record, dataset, specification or author statement.

secondary-source.description: A source that reports on primary sources.

descriptive-statistics.description: Counts, means, distributions, correlations computed on identified data.

statistical-test.description: A pre-specified statistical test with recorded assumptions, effect size and uncertainty.

holdout-evaluation.description: Evaluation on data held out from fitting and selection.

leakage-check.description: Explicit check that no target information leaks into features or splits.

sensitivity-analysis.description: Result recomputed under varied assumptions, subsets or parameters.

observational-data.description: Associations in data that was not produced by an intervention.

controlled-experiment.description: An intervention with a control condition (randomized or otherwise controlled).

causal-design.description: A quasi-experimental design applied with stated identifying assumptions (difference-in-differences, instrumental variable, regression discontinuity, stratification on a measured confounder).

independent-review.description: A critique by an agent or person who did not produce the work under review.

user-report.description: Something the user said they observed. Recorded faithfully, but weak authority for almost every claim type.

function-works.description: A function or unit behaves as specified in a test environment.

works-in-final-package.description: Behavior holds in the built or shipped artifact.

static-reference.description: Something is referenced, declared or present in an artifact (says nothing about execution).

behavior-observed.description: A behavior was observed in execution.

root-cause-identified.description: A specific cause produces the failure: changing it removes the failure and restoring it brings the failure back.

regression-absent.description: Existing behavior still passes after a change.

parser-preserves-file.description: Reading and writing preserves the file.

field-semantics.description: A field in a format means a specific thing.

format-reconstructed.description: A reconstruction reproduces the original behavior on the declared cases.

conjecture-refuted.description: A general claim is false because an explicit counterexample exists.

theorem-valid.description: A general mathematical statement is true.

historical-claim.description: A historical or documentary statement is true.

source-states.description: A specific document states something (not that the statement is true).

correlation-exists.description: Two variables are associated in the identified data.

statistical-difference.description: A difference exceeds what the stated noise model explains.

causal-effect.description: An intervention or variable causes an effect.

model-generalizes.description: A model's measured performance holds on unseen data.

user-reported.description: The user reported something (records the report, not its truth).
